privacy.publishOrTrack: never — C, the sheets and every result stay outside both clones (D-127 §2)

methodDefinition.what: D-232 — D-225's method, with three general corrections: a skin shadow shifts the hue no more than C's own skin shading does (orange fabric over skin is fabric); G-2 counts a base pixel as unchanged only when its chroma is unchanged too (dark fabric shading is no grey remnant); a thin contour line hanging below a hem or a cuff is the limb's redrawn contour, not garment, and FIT-6v2 reports a limb leaving a garment at its end (fitCheck d232). Items are measured against seam-contract-v2

frozen.codeNote: the pipeline code at D-235's authorisation; since D-232 (merge 968d27a) only the item registry (INDEPENDENT_ITEMS) and the sheet CLI's --contract flag changed — re-running D-232's validation manifest gave all 250 output files byte-identical (run.json differs only in the pilot's code hash)
frozen.evaluateWith: a checkout whose IP.codeHashes() equal these; a later method version is never this validation
frozen.afterRun: every new picture is processed with d232 as frozen before anything else; a fault may be documented and investigated, the d232 result is kept; a correction is a new method version and never counts as a validation of d232

request.modelNote: the model of D-207, D-218 and D-228, unchanged; never switched silently — another model is a new decision
request.image2: the reference sheet of the call's category drawn for seam-contract-v2
request.referenceGenerator: node tools/avatar/northstar-item-pilot.mjs --seam-reference <top|bottom|shoes> --contract v2 --out <empty dir> (deterministic; v1 redrawn gives D-228's pins byte for byte)

consistency.sheetsVsContract: the top and bottom sheets are drawn from seam-contract-v2's parameters (the green hip band at shorts ± 6, the magenta hip lines at ± 6); the shoe sheet is byte for byte D-228's (no shoe rule changed)
consistency.promptsVsSheets: each reference sentence names only colours the category's sheet draws (tested on the stand-in); the sentences are D-228's, unchanged
consistency.promptsVsContract: the modelDraws text is v1's and v2's alike: bottoms 'as wide as the grey base shorts' (inside v2's + 6), tops 'at least a finger wider than the shorts' at a station (v2: + 6), the full hem 'just below the ankle … square, wider than the leg' (A + [6, 12], leg ± 10), a boot shaft 'about one hand-width above the ankle, not higher' (A − 56). An item that follows the words meets v2
consistency.knownGap: no words name v2's numbers (a model reads no pixels): the sheet shows them; whether a model reads it is what the experiment tests

differencesFromD228: method d232 (D-228 was evaluated with d225; its frozen verdict stands)
seam-contract-v2's top and bottom sheets (hip lanes ± 6) instead of v1's; the shoe sheet unchanged
new designs, none seen by the method's development: two tops, two bottoms, two closed shoes (D-228: two tops, three bottoms, one boot)

the matrix combines new items with old items that are technically OK under d232, and every planned outfit counts in the denominator, missing or rejected ones included
manual findings are a fifth axis: visible faults no check reports
new call ids, token, claims, stop file and output root; no D-228 permission is reused (all six are spent and closed)
order: N1, N2, N3, N4, N5, N6 — a call is refused unless every earlier call has a claim and a written outcome that does not stop the run
stopRules: credit or access: HTTP 401, 403 or 429, or an error code naming quota or billing
uncertain dispatch: DISPATCHED_RESULT_UNKNOWN, NOT_DISPATCHED, RESPONSE_BODY_UNREADABLE, UNEXPECTED, or a claim without a written outcome
request shape: HTTP 400 that is not a moderation block, or any HTTP 5xx
format: a received picture that is not a 1024x1536 RGBA PNG (TECHNICAL_REJECT at receipt)
the executor's stop file D-235-STOP.json (a common method failure found after a receipt: a registration failure G-1 in two calls, or reference marks drawn into two pictures)
stopProcedure: after each received picture the executor runs `northstar-item-pilot.mjs --process` (method d232, frozen) for that item before the next call and inspects registration, extraction, seams and drawn reference marks. A COMMON METHOD FAILURE — a registration failure G-1 in two calls, or the sheet's marks drawn into two pictures — is written as D-235-STOP.json, which the adapter refuses on. An item-specific failure (a fit fault, a contract break, a technical rejection) never stops the run.

calls.tests: hip seam: a hip-length hem at a station, the hip corners covered, at least shorts + 6 wide (light, skin-near fabric)
long sleeves: the cuff in the cuff band, the hem on the waist line (dark fabric)
trousers / shoes: a full, square hem in A + [6, 12], leg ± 10 (dark fabric)
skirt / top: no line in the hem zone, within shorts + 6 at the hips, cropped (light, skin-near fabric)
a low closed shoe: collar at the ankle, within the leg ± 8 (light, skin-near — next to C's feet)
an ankle boot with a shaft: at most A − 56, within the leg ± 8 (dark)

matrix.oldItemsChosen: technically OK under d232 and the closest to seam-contract-v2 of each category: the tank (waist line), the hip tee V1 (station), the navy shorts and the capri V4 (both comply with v2), the white sneakers (comply)

acceptance.frozen: before any call; never adjusted during or after the experiment

axes.technical: pipeline method d232 as frozen: each new item technically OK or rejected (missing — no picture — counts as rejected)
axes.contract: BC.contractCheck(seam-contract-v2) per new item: every SC rule recorded; targetRules are the ones it was designed to meet
axes.combinationFit: BC.outfitCheck revision d225 on all 48 planned outfits; an outfit with a missing or technically rejected item counts as NOT passing; the findings register applies
axes.manualFindings: the executor inspects every composable outfit with a new item at x2 and at app size and records visible faults no check reports (a double line, a slit, a stray line, a colour fringe, missing fabric); a fault of one item repeated across outfits counts once
axes.visualQuality: the owner's own review — never inferred

acceptance.separation: the five axes are reported apart and never merged per item; a contract break is not by itself a visible fault; a technical or contract pass is not a visual approval

measures.T: new items technically OK under d232, of 6
measures.K: planned outfits passing the outfit check, of 48 (missing / rejected items count as failing)
measures.C: new items meeting all their targetRules under v2, of 6 (reported, not in the decision)
measures.CMF: a common method failure (the stop file)

decision.largerBatch: T ≥ 5 AND K ≥ 39 (≥ 80 % of 48) AND MF = 0 AND no common method failure
decision.fundamentalMethodChange: T ≤ 3 OR K < 24 (< 50 % of 48) OR MF ≥ 3 OR a common method failure
decision.otherwise: a targeted correction (a named rule, as a new method version) and then a new small independent test — no larger batch

failureClasses.generation: the model did not follow the instruction or redrew the body
failureClasses.extraction: the picture has the material, the layer does not (or the reverse)
failureClasses.composition: layer order, covering, shadow or alignment in a combination
failureClasses.contract: a visible fault no rule catches, or a rule break with no visible consequence
failureClasses.check: a check reports a fault the picture does not have, or misses one it has

limits: six designs, one picture each: no estimate of a rate
one model, one figure (C), one prompt template
the old items in the matrix took part in the method's development; only outfits with a new item test it
acceptance.noExpansion: no further calls follow automatically, whatever the result
